Published online:
        Not explicitly stated; references August 12 (2026) as the eclipse date — article appears to be a pre-event guide published ahead of August 12, 2026.
    Geographic focus:
        Europe (Spain, Iceland), Greenland, Arctic/Russia; primary observational focus on Spain and Iceland.
    Temporal focus:
        T1. Historical observation [YES] — references 1999 and 2024 eclipses.
        T2. Forward-looking immediate [YES] — event-specific guide for August 12, 2026.
        T3. Long-term development [YES] — brief mention of 2027 eclipse and Moon's orbital drift over 600M years.
    Synopsis:
        Comprehensive public-interest guide covering the August 12, 2026 total solar eclipse. Covers path of totality (Russia → Greenland → Iceland → Spain), city-level timing, weather outlook (favourable for Spain, poor for Iceland), photography tips, and eye safety. No energy or economic content.
